S2-07_laser_beamed_drone.verdict: KILL: beam is ~400x ocular MPE, every pointing miss lands on a crowded snow surface; a 28 cm skin-safe beam needs a receiver bigger than the drone; and the drone is still a drone (no originality gain).

S2-08_samara_spin_cam.verdict: KILL: global shutter fixes blur (0.16 deg) but monocopter translation (~5 m/s ASSUMED) is below the skier 86 % of the time; rolling-shutter 360 cams skew ~12 deg; efficiency gain does not matter if it cannot keep up.

S2-09_leapfrog_perch.verdict: KILL: overtaking a 12 m/s skier needs ~19 m/s (KE 26 J at 150 g, or <=85 g airframe that cannot fly 19 m/s in wind); only static pass-by shots; lands on piste in others' line.

S2-10_micro_ski_robot.verdict: KILL: 0.2 m camera height sees boots and snow spray; ruts/moguls exceed body size; others ski over it; stopping on 20 deg needs ~50 m even with a claw. Same physics as round-1 BODY-09/10.

S2-11_battery_quad.self_heating: -20->0 C in 20 s using 3.8 % capacity (Penn State/EC Power 2016)
S2-11_battery_quad.verdict: ENABLER, not a concept: Si-anode roughly triples cold flight time (~12->~40 min at 25 W, if the 450 Wh/kg cells deliver ~1C in the cold, unverified) of a palm follow drone, still < 45 min and still the market product the user rejected. Used inside S2-01/S2-02.

S2-12_guided_parafoil.verdict: KILL as stand-alone: glide 18.4 deg means it sinks into any slope flatter than 18 deg and cannot climb; landing miss ~13 m (Georgia Tech) vs 3 m pickup need. Keep soft-wing idea as a safety skin for S2-01.

S2-13_ground_effect_skim.verdict: KILL: needs h < ~0.3 m above snow (span 0.62 m) in the band where other skiers' skis and legs are; moguls and rollers exceed h. Induced-drag saving is irrelevant because gravity already pays.

S2-14_tether_trolley.verdict: KILL: any point on a taut line through the skier sees him from the same elevation; moving the camera inward only shrinks distance, it cannot lower the view angle.

S2-15_micro_swarm.verdict: KILL: sub-100 g rotorcraft top out ~10 m/s (Black Hornet 4, 70 g) so they lose the skier ~47 % of the time; swarm multiplies regulatory and recovery burden.

S2-16_boomerang_cam.verdict: KILL: returns to the throw point, not to a moving skier (~29 m behind); spin 10 Hz gives 29 deg rolling-shutter skew; catch with gloves unreliable.
